title: Austin Man Pleads Guilty to Making Violent Threats Against FBI Director and Employees
body: Press Release Austin Man Pleads Guilty to Making Violent Threats Against FBI Director and Employees Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas AUSTIN, Texas – An Austin man pleaded guilty in federal court this week to one count of interstate communications with threat to injure or kidnap, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents, June 7, Michael James Argo, 46, used the social media platform X to make several public threats to injure and murder FBI Director Kash Patel and FBI employees. An FBI agent contacted Argo about the threats on July 30. Despite being aware of the investigation into his June threats, Argo again used his X account between Sept. 13 and Sept. 18 to make additional public threats to injure, murder and kidnap Patel. A criminal complaint filed on Sept. 20 includes multiple threatening posts from Argo’s X profile. One post threatens to “kidnap and gender reassign” Patel. Other posts include photos in which Argo was brandishing a firearm. He also threatened the agent who had initially contacted him regarding the investigation based on his threats in June. Argo faces up to five years in federal prison, three years of supervised release and a maximum fine of $250,000. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. The FBI is investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Britni Verdeja is prosecuting the case. ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Texas, Western

title: Jefferson County Man Sentenced to Over 21 Years in Prison for Receipt and  Possession of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Jefferson County Man Sentenced to Over 21 Years in Prison for Receipt and  Possession of Child Pornography Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov James Yerdon, age 56, of Adams Center, New York, was sentenced Monday, November 9, 2026, in federal court to 262 months in federal prison for receiving and possessing child pornography. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III, Anthony Patrone, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), and New York State Police (NYSP) Superintendent Steven G. James made the announcement. As part of his prior guilty plea, Yerdon, a previously convicted sex offender, admitted that on May 13, 2025, he possessed multiple images and videos of child pornography that he had downloaded from the internet including material depicting the sexual abuse of children as young as five months old. The defendant also possessed nude images of a 7-year-old child Yerdon had created during a trip Yerdon took with the child to the Albany, New York area. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sarcone stated: “The defendant’s conduct in this case is horrific and is deserving of the lengthy sentence imposed today. The defendant is a repeat offender who not only sought out and accumulated child pornography online, but he also directly targeted children in our community. I am grateful to HSI and the New York State Police for their tireless work protecting our communities and especially our children from predators like the defendant.” NYSP Superintendent Steven G. James said, “Mr. Yerdon had no regard for his victims or their well-being, instead he took advantage of them in the most deplorable manner. This case serves as a reminder that those who prey on vulnerable and defenseless individuals, especially when they are in a place of trust, will be fully prosecuted. The State Police is committed to our partnership with the United States Attorney’s Office and Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations to intercept these predators and bring an end to the damage they inflict.” In addition to the term of imprisonment, Chief U.S. District Judge, Brenda K. Sannes, also sentenced Yerdon to serve a 20-year term of supervised release, to begin after Yerdon is released from prison, at which time Yerdon will also be required to register as a sex offender. Yerdon was also ordered to pay $26,000 in restitution to victims of his offense. The case was investigated by HSI and NYSP and was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Adrian LaRochelle as part of Project Safe Childhood. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Northern

body: Press Release Medina County Man Sentenced to 17 Years in Prison for Receipt, Distribution, and Possession of Child Pornography Charges Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Ohio YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio – A 39-year-old repeat offender has been sentenced to federal prison for child pornography charges. Nicholas Keith Sutherland, of Medina, was sentenced to 210 months (17.5 years) in prison by U.S. District Judge Benita Y. Pearson after pleading guilty in May to: •    Receipt and Distribution of Visual Depictions of Real Minors Engaged in Sexually Explicit Conduct •    Transportation of Visual Depictions of Minors Engaged in Sexually Explicit Conduct •    Possession of Child Pornography Sutherland was also ordered to serve 15 years of supervised release after imprisonment and pay $15,000 toward the Justice for Victims of Trafficking Act, which was established in 2015 to provide justice for victims of trafficking, and $30,000 toward the Amy, Vicky, and Andy Child Pornography Assistance Act which was established in 2018 to provide monetary assistance for victims of child sexual abuse. Additionally, he was ordered to pay $30,000 in restitution to the victims. According to court documents, law enforcement was investigating suspected Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) activity on an online platform and Sutherland was subsequently identified. Pursuant to a federal search warrant, his vehicle, person, and residence were searched.  Electronic devices and printed photographs of child pornography were discovered.  Sutherland was found to be in possession of over 1,300 images of child pornography. This was Sutherland’s fourth conviction for child pornography charges, having previously been convicted in 2013 for Illegal Use of a Minor in a Nudity Oriented Material, in 2014 for Pandering Sexually Oriented Material Involving a Minor, and in 2018 for Pandering Obscenity Involving a Minor. The investigation was led by the FBI Akron Resident Agency, Medina Police Department and the Ohio Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force. Assistant United States Attorneys Joseph P. Dangelo and Nicolette Drotos led the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. Employee at Major International Law Firm Charged With Insider Trading
body: Press Release Employee at Major International Law Firm Charged With Insider Trading Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of New York Defendant Repeatedly Traded in Advance of Public Announcements Related to Major Transactions Involving Law Firm’s Clients Listed on NYSE and NASDAQ Earlier today, in federal court in Brooklyn, a criminal complaint was unsealed charging Chetram Balli, also known as “Tony Balli,” with insider trading in the shares of five companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and NASDAQ.  Balli was arrested this morning in Queens, New York, and is scheduled to appear this afternoon before United States Magistrate Judge Marcia M. Henry for his initial appearance and arraignment.  As alleged in the criminal complaint, Balli misused material non-public information (MNPI) related to the law firm’s clients to trade ahead of major mergers and acquisitions.  The criminal complaint alleges that Balli made over $70,000 in profit on his trades between April 2025 and October 2026. Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, and James C. Barnacle, Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, New York Field Office (FBI), announced the arrest and charges. “As alleged, Balli repeatedly traded on inside information that he misappropriated from his employer and his employer’s clients,” stated United States Attorney Nocella.  “Our Office is committed to protecting the integrity of the securities markets and investors who play by the rules.  Corrupt individuals who might be tempted to take advantage of their access to confidential information should know that we are watching.” Mr. Nocella expressed his appreciation to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) Regulatory Operations – Surveillance for their significant assistance in the investigation. “Chetram Balli allegedly turned privileged access into an illegal advantage, repeatedly trading securities ahead of public announcements involving major corporate transactions.  By misappropriating confidential information for personal profit, he gained an unfair edge over law-abiding investors and compromised the fairness that our markets depend upon.  May these charges act as a warning to others, that material non-public information cannot be used for personal gain, and if it is, the FBI will follow the trail of deceit to the finish line,” stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle. As alleged, since approximately 1989, Balli worked as a Document Processing Specialist at Law Firm-1, a major international law firm based in New York City that maintains multiple practice areas including a mergers and acquisitions practice.  As part of his employment, Balli supported attorneys by creating and revising complex legal documents, and preparing and submitting filings through the SEC’s Electronic Data gathering, Analysis and Retrieval (EDGAR) system.  Balli, who was prohibited by Law Firm-1’s policies from trading on MNPI learned in the course of his duties, used his access to non-public client information relating to upcoming partnerships, mergers, and planned acquisitions, to trade in at least five NYSE-listed or NASDAQ-listed companies. For example, as alleged in the complaint, on May 12, 2025, Balli purchased approximately 14,866 shares in E2open Parent Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: ETWO), a Texas-based provider of supply chain management software.  Balli had not previously invested in ETWO shares.  Less than two weeks later, on May 25, 2025, WiseTech Global Limited, a leading provider of software solutions for the global trade, logistics, and supply chain industries based in Australia, announced that it had entered into an agreement to acquire E2open in an all-cash transaction for $3.30 per share equating to an enterprise value of $2.1 billion.  That share price represented a 28% premium to the closing price of ETWO shares on the previous trading day.  Law Firm-1 represented WiseTech in connection with its acquisition of E2open.  Balli subsequently sold his entire ETWO position on May 27, 2025, the first trading day after the WiseTech acquisition was announced. The complaint alleged similar trading by Balli in Forge Global Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: FRGE) in advance of the November 2025 announcement of its acquisition by the Charles Schwab Corporation for $660 million; Paramount Skydance Corp. (NASDAQ: PSKY) in advance of the February 2026 announcement of its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. for $110 billion; Talkspace, Inc. (NASDAQ: TALK) in advance of the March 2026 announcement of its acquisition by Universal Health Services, Inc. for $853 million; and Pacira BioSciences, Inc. (NYSE: PCRX) in advance of the October 2026 announcement of its acquisition by Viatris Inc. for $1.65 billion. The charges in the complaint are allegations and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.  If convicted of the charges in the complaint, Balli faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. The government’s case is being handled by the Office’s Business and Securities Fraud Section.  Assistant United States  Attorneys Jonathan P. Lax and Nick M. Axelrod are in charge of the prosecution, with assistance from Paralegal Specialist Melina Piatti-Chayan. The Defendant : CHETRAM BALLI Age:  54 Hollis, Queens E.D.N.Y. title: Convictions through Guilty Verdict, Pleas and Sentencings in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecutions
body: Press Release Convictions through Guilty Verdict, Pleas and Sentencings in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecutions Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Puerto Rico, Héctor Ramírez-Carbó, Acting United States Attorney, in conjunction with our partner agencies in the Homeland Security Task Force (“HSTF”) announce the following prosecutorial results for October 30, and the week of November 2 through November 6, 2026. The HSTF is a permanent, interagency law enforcement task force created by executive order to combat transnational criminal organizations—including cartels, trafficking networks, and foreign terrorist organizations. Conviction through Guilty Verdict: On Friday, October 30, 2026, defendant Jonathan Radhames Vicente-Ramírez, was found guilty by a jury at trial of conspiracy to import 160 kilograms of cocaine, importation of cocaine and jettisoning bales of cocaine. The defendant remains detained in federal custody pending his sentence on January 25, 2027, before the Honorable Aida Delgado-Colon.  AUSA’s Luis A. Valentín and Ana Mercado Roque represented the United States at trial. Convictions through Guilty Pleas: On November 2, 2026, Jhonattan Rodríguez-Gutiérrez pleaded guilty to Count One of the Indictment in Criminal Case 21-317 (PAD). According to the indictment, the defendant was charged for conspiring to possess with intent to distribute 225 kilograms of cocaine aboard a vessel subject to the jurisdiction of the United States. Defendant was arrested in Colombia and extradited to Puerto Rico on June 13, 2024. The Court scheduled defendant’s sentencing hearing for February 5, 2027. AUSA Camille García Jiménez is in charge of the prosecution of the case. On November 3, 2026, Carlos Javier Ruiz-Patiño, a/k/a “Hustler Man/Jordan/El Chamo”, pleaded guilty to money laundering conspiracy and narcotics importation conspiracy in Criminal Case 23-85 (PAD). According to the Superseding Indictment, the defendant was charged with conspiring to launder money from the sale of controlled substances, several specific money laundering events, conspiring to import cocaine into the United States, aiding and abetting narcotics importation, and conspiring to possess with intent to distribute cocaine.  Defendant was arrested on March 13, 2023. The court set defendant’s sentencing date for February 5, 2027. AUSA Lani Lear is in charge of the prosecution of the case. On November 3, 2026, Yeicol Lebrón-Gamboa pleaded guilty to Count One in Criminal Case 25-274 (CVR). According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with aiding and abetting others known and unknown to knowingly and intentionally possess with intent to distribute cocaine and distribute 5 kilograms or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of cocaine, aboard a vessel subject to the jurisdiction of the United States.  Defendant was arrested on December 15, 2025. The court set defendant’s sentencing date for February 1, 2027. SAUSAs Edwin Cabán Jr. and Cody A. McKiney are in charge of the prosecution of the case. On November 4, 2026, Ashraf Sobirovich Hashimov pleaded guilty to marriage fraudin criminal case no. 26-335 (RAM). According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with conspiracy to commit marriage fraud and a marriage fraud offense. Defendant was arrested on September 15, 2026. Defendant was sentenced to time served to be followed by a term of supervised release of two years. AUSA Steven Liong-Rodríguez is in charge of the prosecution of the case. Sentencings: On November 2, 2026, Brian Torres-Santana was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Francisco A. Besosa to 33 months of imprisonment and 5 years of supervised release for possessing with intent to distribute 5 kilograms or more of cocaine. According to court documents, defendant was indicted on March 5, 2026, in Criminal Case 26-081(FAB), and pleaded guilty on July 21, 2026. AUSA Antonio López is in charge of the prosecution of the case. On November 3, 2026, Amrit Amed Quijano-Rosado was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Camille Vélez-Rivé to 78 months of imprisonment for possessing with intent to distribute 5 kilograms or more of cocaine aboard a vessel subject to the jurisdiction of the United States. According to court documents, defendant was indicted on August 7, 2025, in Criminal Case 25-347(CVR), and pleaded guilty on June 2, 2026. AUSA Antonio López is in charge of the prosecution of the case. On November 4, 2026, Ezequiel Olivo-Bido was sentenced by United States District Court Silvia Carreño Coll to 204 months (17 years) of imprisonment for conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances. According to court documents, defendant was indicted on June 10, 2025, in Criminal Case 25-272 (SCC) and pleaded guilty on July 17, 2026. AUSAs Laura Díaz-González and Andrés Orr are in charge of the prosecution of the case. On November 5, 2026, Jean C. Fernández-Garay, a/k/a “Logan/Bebo” was sentenced by United States District Court Judge María Angongiorgi-Jordán to five (5) years of imprisonment to be followed by six (6) years of supervised release for his participation in a violent drug trafficking organization that worked out of various Public Housing Projects in the Carolina and San Juan areas, principally the Sabana Abajo Public Housing Project. According to court documents, defendant was indicted on December 5, 2024, in Criminal Case 24-453 (MAJ), and pleaded guilty on May 27, 2026. The defendant also received one (1) year of incarceration for violating the terms of his supervised release in cases 12-678 and 16-440; this additional year will run consecutively to the time he will serve in case 24-453. AUSAs Laura Díaz González and Joseph Russell are in charge of the prosecution of the case. On November 6, 2026, Alejandro Saenz-Escobar, a/k/a “Fresa/Fresita/Andito,” was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Gina Méndez-Miró to 173 months (14 years and 5 months) and 23 days of imprisonment to be followed by 10 years of supervised release for participating in a drug trafficking organization that operated in and around the Manatí area, and principally out of the Enrique Zorilla Public Housing Project. According to court documents, defendant was indicted on September 20, 2023, in Criminal Case 23-353 (GMM), and pleaded guilty on August 21, 2026. The defendant was also sentenced to 8 months of incarceration in case 25-475 for possessing controlled substances in MDC Guaynabo. AUSAs Joseph Russell, Andrés Orr and Daphne Cordero are in charge of the prosecution of the cases. These prosecutions are part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF San Juan comprises agents and officers from the following federal partners: FBI, ICE-HSI, CBP (OFO, AMO and Border Patrol), the U.S. Marshals Service for Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, DEA, ATF, IRS, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the Department of State, and the U.S. Secret Service, the Puerto Rico/U.S. Virgin Islands HIDTA, TSA, FAA, and the U.S. Attorney’s Offices for the Districts of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The HSTF also has the following state and local law enforcement partners as participating agencies: the Puerto Rico Police Department; the San Juan, Carolina, Guaynabo, Barceloneta, and Ponce Municipal Police Departments, the Puerto Rico National Guard – Counter Drug Program; the Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation; the Puerto Rico Internal Revenue Service (Hacienda); the Puerto Rico Port Authority; and the Virgin Islands Police Department. ### Updated November 12, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Drug Trafficking Fraud Firearms Offenses Immigration Violent Crime Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Puerto Rico U.S. Marshals Service Press Release Number: 2026-121

title: A Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Results in Brookland Man Being Sentenced to 12 Years in Federal Prison for Trafficking Methamphetamine
body: Press Release A Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Results in Brookland Man Being Sentenced to 12 Years in Federal Prison for Trafficking Methamphetamine Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Arkansas Ms. Paulette Chappelle, Public Affairs Officer paulette.chappelle@usdoj.gov JONESBORO—Rickey Allen Brown was sentenced to 144 months in federal prison for distribution of methamphetamine and possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine. Jonathan D. Ross, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas, announced the sentenced which was handed down today by United States District Judge D.P. Marshall, Jr. On May 2, 2025, a Superseding Information was filed charging Brown, 56, of Brookland, with one count of distribution of 50 grams or more, but less than 500 grams, of methamphetamine and one count of possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more, but less than 500 grams, of methamphetamine. On that same day the Superseding Information was filed, Brown pleaded guilty to the Superseding Information. Judge Marshall also sentenced Brown to five years’ supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. An investigation revealed that on December 27, 2021, a confidential informant (CI) conducted a controlled buy of two bags of methamphetamine from Brown at his residence in Brookland. The CI, in exchange for over 50 grams of methamphetamine, paid Brown $700 and provided the methamphetamine to law enforcement officers. The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Laboratory confirmed the purity of the methamphetamine at 100%. On January 27, 2022, law enforcement officers conducted surveillance on a known drug house. During the surveillance, officers observed a Kia Optima pull up and park on the street outside the residence with Brown exiting the vehicle and entering the residence. Brown briefly remained in the residence and when he exited to get in his vehicle, was observed walking as though he was attempting to conceal an item. Once Brown drove away, officers conducted a traffic stop after observing Brown committing traffic violations. While talking to Brown, officers observed him sweating profusely and his hands were shaking, and officers smelled marijuana. During a search, officers located two bags of methamphetamine in Brown’s pocket. When officers searched Brown’s vehicle, they located a canvas bag underneath the driver’s seat that contained close to 110 grams of 100% pure methamphetamine. Brown’s criminal history includes convictions for possession of drug paraphernalia with intent to use, second degree stalking, manufacture of methamphetamine, domestic battery third degree, first degree assault, second degree assault on family or household member, and terroristic threatening. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Little Rock comprises agents and officers from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Arkansas State Police, Second Judicial Drug Task Force, and the Craighead County Sheriff’s Office with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Arkansas. This case was investigated by the FBI with assistance from the Second Judicial Drug Task Force, Craighead County Sheriff’s Office, and the Arkansas State Police. This case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Erin O’Leary. # # # Additional information about the office of the United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas, is available online at https://www.justice.gov/edar X (formerly known as Twitter): @USAO_EDAR Updated November 12, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Arkansas, Eastern

title: Long Island Man Convicted of Crimes Against Children, Including Sexual Exploitation and Receipt of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Long Island Man Convicted of Crimes Against Children, Including Sexual Exploitation and Receipt of Child Pornography Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of New York Earlier today, a federal jury in Central Islip convicted Jacob Israel Walden on all eight counts of a superseding indictment charging him with sexual exploitation of children, receipt of child pornography, possession of child pornography, and access with intent to view child pornography.  The verdict followed a three-day trial before United States District Judge Gary R. Brown.  When sentenced, Walden faces a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years’ imprisonment and up to life imprisonment. Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, and Michael S. McCarthy, Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations, New Jersey (HSI New Jersey), announced the verdict. “Walden paid children to create sexually explicit images and videos for his own gratification,” stated United States Attorney Nocella.  “Today’s verdict holds him accountable for exploiting those children.  I thank the victims who came forward and testified about his depraved conduct.” As proven at trial, law enforcement identified Walden, a Long Island resident and healthcare executive, as a repeat purchaser of child sexual abuse material from an online production and distribution ring. Walden also used social media and encrypted messaging services to communicate with minors and induce them to produce sexually explicit images and videos of themselves in exchange for money. Walden provided step-by-step instructions to his victims about the content they should produce for him, insisted that they address him as “daddy,” and sent electronic payments after receiving the requested material.  He also used his minor victims to recruit other minors for his gratification.  The evidence also showed that Walden purchased child sexual abuse material from the internet and stored it on his cellphone. This prosecution is part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide Department of Justice initiative to combat child sexual exploitation and abuse.  The initiative brings together federal, state and local resources to identify and rescue victims and investigate and prosecute those who exploit children. For more information, visit https://www.justice.gov/psc. The government’s case is being handled by the Criminal Section of the Office’s Long Island Division.  Trial Attorney Leonid Sandlar and Assistant United States Attorney Michael D. Manzo are in charge of the prosecution, with the assistance of Paralegal Specialists David Harrison and Adam Bernard. The Defendant : JACOB ISRAEL WALDEN Age: 40 Valley Stream, New York E.D.N.Y. title: Cold Case Solved, Tulsa Man Sentenced to 50 Years for Planned Violent Robbery That Claimed a Young Life
body: Press Release Cold Case Solved, Tulsa Man Sentenced to 50 Years for Planned Violent Robbery That Claimed a Young Life Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Oklahoma TULSA, Okla. – A U.S. District Judge Gregory K. Frizzell sentenced Jamalo Bruner Jr. to 50 years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, for using a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence that resulted in the death of Benjamin Montgomery. Bruner previously pleaded guilty to the federal offense. According to court records, on October 10, 2019, Bruner and another armed participant planned to rob Aaron Pritchard of marijuana. Armed with 9mm pistols, the pair waited for Pritchard at the Bellevue Apartments in Tulsa before confronting him at gunpoint. During the robbery, Pritchard was struck in the head with a pistol and ordered to take the assailants to an apartment. When Pritchard was unable to locate a key to the intended apartment, he went to a neighboring apartment occupied by Benjamin Montgomery. Bruner and his accomplice forced their way inside while continuing to hold Pritchard at gunpoint. As they entered the apartment, a shot was fired through the front door and into the ceiling. Montgomery was inside the apartment with five friends when the armed intruders entered. In an effort to protect those in the apartment, Montgomery confronted the gunmen. During the ensuing struggle, Montgomery was shot in the chest and killed. Bruner and his accomplice fled the scene. Although investigators were unable to determine which participant fired the fatal shot, the evidence established Bruner's active role in the armed robbery and firearm offense that resulted in Montgomery's death. The homicide remained unsolved for several years until investigators with the FBI and the Tulsa Police Department Homicide Unit developed new leads and reopened the case. DNA testing conducted during the investigation produced a profile consistent with Bruner's DNA, helping investigators connect him to the crime. At sentencing, Montgomery's family members and friends spoke about the lasting impact of his death and the years of grief they have endured. Family members said they were grateful for the work of law enforcement and prosecutors and believed justice had been served. Montgomery had celebrated his 22nd birthday just three days before his death. Family members described him as a loyal son, devoted brother, trusted friend, athlete, animal lover, and a young man known for protecting others and helping those in need. His mother recalled that he regularly showed compassion to strangers, cared deeply for animals, and remained exceptionally close to his family. Loved ones remembered him as someone who instinctively stood up for others and whose final actions reflected the courage and selflessness that defined his life. "Jamalo Bruner helped orchestrate a violent armed robbery and set in motion the chain of events that took Benjamin Montgomery's life," said U.S. Attorney Christopher J. Nassar. “The 50-year federal sentence is a just and significant punishment for a senseless crime that devastated a family and shocked our community. Benjamin was only 22 years old. His loved ones described a young man known for his compassion and willingness to protect others. On the night he was killed, he did exactly that, confronting armed intruders in an effort to protect his friends. While no sentence can restore Benjamin’s stolen future or erase the pain his family has carried for years, today's outcome delivers meaningful justice." “The defendant’s actions resulted in the tragic death of a young man and forever changed the lives of his family and loved ones. This sentence reflects the serious consequences of those actions,” said FBI Oklahoma City Special Agent in Charge Doug Goodwater. “The FBI remains committed to pursuing justice on behalf of all victims of violence, and the families who bear the impact of these senseless crimes.” Assistant U.S. Attorney Tyson McCoy prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States. The FBI and the Tulsa Police Department Homicide Unit investigated the case. The United States Attorney's Office would like to recognize the efforts of Tulsa Police Department Detective Lacy Lansdown who led the investigation that ultimately solved the cold case, and recognize the valuable assistance provided by Tulsa Police Department Homicide Unit Case Support Specialist Margot Heyne-Bell. Project Safe Neighborhoods focuses on the most pressing violent crime issues facing our communities. This nationwide initiative brings together federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement and prosecutors to strategically address and reduce violent crime, in collaboration with other agencies and organizations that serve communities. Florida Missionary Indicted for Child Exploitation Crimes in Haiti
body: Press Release Florida Missionary Indicted for Child Exploitation Crimes in Haiti Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida returned an indictment charging Thomas Osbeck, 70, of Ft. Myers, Florida, with engaging in, and attempting to engage in, illicit sexual conduct with minors in Haiti. According to court documents, Osbeck routinely traveled from the United States to Haiti over the past three decades and sexually abused minors in that country. Osbeck was the founder of Jesus in Haiti Ministries and later Ignite Your Faith Ministries, through which he took in vulnerable children throughout the country. The charges in the indictment are based on his sexual abuse of a Haitian boy between approximately 2004 and 2008, when the boy was approximately 8 through 12 years old, and his attempt to engage in a commercial sex act around 2019-2020 with another Haitian boy. Osbeck was taken into custody in Haiti at the end of September 2026 after an investigation by Haitian authorities and then returned to the United States on Oct. 14 where he was arrested by U.S. law enforcement upon landing at Miami International Airport. He has remained in custody since that time. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division; Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas for the Southern District of Florida; and Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement. FBI Miami is investigating the case. Trial Attorney Jessica L. Urban of the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS) and Assistant U.S. Attorney Abbie D. Waxman for the Southern District of Florida are prosecuting the case. Investigators believe Osbeck has victimized additional children. If you believe you may be a victim of Osbeck or have other information that could further law enforcement’s investigation, you are encouraged to contact OsBeckInfo@fbi.gov . This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, visit www.justice.gov/psc . An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: Man Who Allegedly Trafficked Cocaine in Chicago Arrested in Argentina and Extradited to United States
body: Press Release Man Who Allegedly Trafficked Cocaine in Chicago Arrested in Argentina and Extradited to United States Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Illinois CHICAGO — A man who allegedly trafficked cocaine in Chicago has been arrested in Argentina and extradited to the United States to face federal drug conspiracy charges in the Northern District of Illinois. RODOLFO AGUIRRE, 38, was originally arrested in Chicago in December 2016 after allegedly conspiring to sell approximately 7,000 grams of cocaine outside of a hotel in the city’s Uptown neighborhood, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court in Chicago. Unbeknownst to Aguirre, the buyer was an undercover law enforcement agent, the complaint states.  Aguirre was released on bond conditions, but he failed to appear in federal court ahead of his scheduled trial in 2017. Aguirre was recently arrested in Argentina and extradited to the United States last week.  He is scheduled to appear in federal court in Chicago on Nov. 17, 2026, at 10:15 a.m., before U.S. District Judge John J. Tharp, Jr.  The government will be seeking Aguirre’s continued detention pending trial. The charges and extradition were announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, and Todd C. Smith, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Field Division of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration.  The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Spitulnik. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs worked with the Government of Argentina to secure the Nov. 6, 2026, extradition of Aguirre. The public is reminded that charges are not evidence of guilt.  The defendant is presumed innocent and entitled to a fair trial at which the government has the burden of proving guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. aguirre_et_al_indictment.pdf aguirre_et_al_complaint.pdf Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Components Criminal - Office of International Affairs Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - Illinois, Northern

title: Miami Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for Threatening Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Former Special Envoy Kristi Noem
body: Press Release Miami Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for Threatening Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Former Special Envoy Kristi Noem Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Florida MIAMI – A Miami man has been sentenced to federal prison for posting online threats targeting Secretary of State Marco Rubio and former Department of State Special Envoy Kristi Noem. U.S. District Judge Beth Bloom sentenced Jon Christopher Enriquez, 47, of Miami, to 24 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to three counts of transmitting threats through interstate communications. “Anyone who believes they can hide behind a keyboard while threatening to kill our nation's leaders should think again,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas for the Southern District of Florida. “These are not harmless words. They are serious federal crimes with serious consequences. We will work relentlessly with our law enforcement partners to identify, prosecute, and bring to justice those who make such threats.” According to court records, on May 27, Enriquez published three posts on the social media platform X threatening Secretary Rubio and Noem, who was then serving as Special Envoy for the Shield of the Americas. The threats were made in three separate public posts over the course of the afternoon. Among other things, the posts threatened that both officials would be executed at specific times. Acting U.S. Attorney Lorenzo Klukas and Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary for Diplomatic Security and Director of the Diplomatic Security Service Nicholas Collura made the announcement. The Diplomatic Security Service investigated the case, with assistance from the Naval Criminal Investigative Service, the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, the City of Miami Police Department, and the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicholas Y. Carré prosecuted the case. Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case number 26-cr-20239. ### Contact Public Affairs Unit U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of Florida USAFLS.News@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Component USAO - Florida, Southern

title: Justice Department Announces Actions to Disrupt North Korea’s Massive Theft of Cryptocurrency
body: Press Release Justice Department Announces Actions to Disrupt North Korea’s Massive Theft of Cryptocurrency Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs North Korean Super Intelligence-Enabled Social Engineering Campaign Known as “FaceStealer” Targeted Cryptocurrency Holders and Individuals Working the Open-Source Supply Chain Today the Department of Justice announced coordinated actions against the Democratic People’s Republic of North Korea (DPRK) government’s schemes to fund its regime through the massive theft of cryptocurrency. These actions include the seizure of cloud-based infrastructure used in the FaceStealer social engineering scheme that has resulted in the theft of more than $400 million worth of cryptocurrency and the court-authorized seizure and restraint of more than $1.2 billion worth of cryptocurrency recently stolen from Binance, a virtual currency exchange. “North Korea’s government bankrolls its rogue regime and illicit weapons program through cryptocurrency theft,” said Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor. “Today’s announcement shows that America will fight back against that corrupt regime’s effort to profit through cybercrime. The National Security Division will use every tool at its disposal to seize and return North Korea’s ill-gotten gains.” “The Criminal Division, specifically the Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section (CCIPS), and our law enforcement partners played the critical role in immediately freezing billions of dollars’ worth of stolen Binance digital assets before they got beyond law enforcement reach,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “As the Department’s liaison to the digital asset industry, the Criminal Division quickly and efficiently used its expertise to immediately halt about half of this historic breach.” “Cryptocurrency unfortunately has become fertile ground for North Korea to defraud victims and fund its malign activities,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California. “Today’s seizure shows that America will continue the fight against rogue states who financially gain from cybercrime.” “By springing into action at a moment’s notice, we worked together to freeze this massive criminal fraud in its tracks,” said U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro for the District of Columbia. “The North Korean regime may think they are sophisticated cyber criminals, but we have consistently met them head on, as we did here seizing more than $1.2 billion of their stolen assets.” “The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years,” said FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman. “North Korean cyber actors have used the FaceStealer scheme to aggressively target individuals in the cryptocurrency and Web3 sectors through deceptive social engineering tactics, resulting in the theft of more than $400 million in the last 18 months. The FBI remains committed to identifying, disrupting, and imposing cost on North Korean actors targeting the virtual asset community.” “North Korea’s FaceStealer is a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user” said Assistant Director in Charge Patrick Grandy of the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office. “It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships. If you can’t imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough. The FBI is sounding the alarm to elevate awareness of this growing scheme, now aimed not only at crypto theft, but also the exploitation of the of the open-source software supply chain.” Seizure of FaceStealer Infrastructure – Central District of California Today, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California announced the disruption of cloud-based infrastructure used by North Korean hackers in a highly effective social engineering scheme that the FBI is calling “FaceStealer.” The scheme, which relies on surreptitiously recorded videos and artificial deepfakes, has resulted in the theft of more than $400 million in the last 18 months and the attempted compromise of individuals involved in the open-source software supply chain. North Korean hackers known publicly by the names Sapphire Sleet, UNC1069, Dangerous Password, CryptoCore, Advanced Persistent Threat 38 (APT38), BlueNoroff, and Stardust Chollima have lured targets with invitations to video meetings delivered from accounts stolen from prior victims. Once a target joins the meeting, the hackers record the target’s webcam video and play a prerecorded video of a previous victim or victims known to the target, thereby simulating the participation of trusted contacts in the meeting to gain the target’s trust. The North Korean hackers also use super intelligence (SI) to develop deepfake videos of well-known and influential individuals often in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries that make the FaceStealer scheme even more effective. Here again, they use the deepfake videos in the meetings with targets to gain the target’s trust. During the meeting, the hackers then introduce a fake technical error into the meeting, such as claiming that the target cannot be heard, and provide a link or prompt to fix the error. The “fix” surreptitiously installs malware on the target’s computer. With the target’s computer compromised, the hackers can steal cryptocurrency or exploit the target’s access to other computer infrastructure. In several reported cases, the hackers stole cryptocurrency and hijacked communication accounts several months to more than a year after the initial compromise. As part of the scheme the hackers also accessed the new victim’s contact lists, social media, and communications apps to target the victim’s personal and professional contacts. The North Korean hackers target individuals working in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries. Additionally, they have increasingly targeted individuals involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software with the FaceStealer technique, attempting to gain access to their devices and the software repository accounts they control. This targeting appears calculated to enable software supply-chain attacks. Pursuant to a federal warrant, the FBI seized over 900 webcam videos of FaceStealer victims. The FBI today published a report providing greater detail on the mechanics of the FaceStealer scheme, including best practices to protect against this scheme and steps victims can take in the event of a compromise. Additionally, the FBI created a website, www.fbi.gov/facestealer , to serve as a centralized hub for resources and information on the scheme. The effort to disrupt the FaceStealer campaign was led by Assistant U.S. Attorney Khaldoun Shobaki for the Central District of California and the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office. The Department, FBI, and Law Enforcement Partners Interdict More Than a Billion Dollars Worth of Virtual Assets Stolen From Binance Separately from the FaceStealer campaign, on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as “TraderTraitor” stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from the Binance cryptocurrency exchange. Since the theft, the National Security Division’s National Security Cyber Section, the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia, and law enforcement partners have worked closely with virtual asset service providers (VASPs) to interdict the stolen assets. Collective U.S. government and private sector efforts so far have resulted in the freeze of more than $2.7 billion, with the Department having already obtained court-authorization to seize or restrain in excess of $1.2 billion of that amount. Efforts to trace, freeze, seize, and forfeit the stolen virtual assets are ongoing, as TraderTraitor actors continue to launder such assets through various cryptocurrency bridges, mixers, and exchanges. For example, last week, the FBI, in coordination with its law enforcement partners at the U.S. Secret Service (USSS) and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS-CI), issued a Cyber Alert attributing the theft and urging VASPs to block transactions with or derived from cryptocurrency addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder the stolen Binance assets. The FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office, Cyber Division, and Virtual Asset Unit are coordinating the FBI’s efforts to recover the stolen virtual assets, working in partnership with the USSS and the IRS-CI. Updated November 12, 2026 Topics Cybercrime National Security Components Criminal - Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) National Security Division (NSD) USAO - California, Central USAO - District of Columbia Press Release Number: 26-1356
retained_feed_body: Today the Department of Justice announced coordinated actions against the Democratic People’s Republic of North Korea (DPRK) government’s schemes to fund its regime through the massive theft of cryptocurrency.

title: Mexican Drug Trafficker Pleads Guilty Using Minors, Aircraft to Smuggle Drugs into the United States
body: Press Release Mexican Drug Trafficker Pleads Guilty Using Minors, Aircraft to Smuggle Drugs into the United States Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California SAN DIEGO – Marco Antonio Lopez-Guerrero, who was previously extradited from Mexico to the United States, pleaded guilty in federal court today following a Homeland Security Task Force investigation to charges of conspiring to import methamphetamine. According to the plea agreement, Lopez-Guerrero led a Mexico-based drug trafficking organization that recruited juvenile girls and young adult women to smuggle methamphetamine into the United States. Lopez-Guerrero also admitted that his organization flew methamphetamine and fentanyl over the border in ultra-light aircraft. Lopez-Guerrero admitted that his organization smuggled more than 180 kilograms of methamphetamine, 19 kilograms of fentanyl, and two kilograms of heroin into the United States. Lopez-Guerrero also admitted to orchestrating the smuggling of money, guns, and ammunition from the United States to Mexico. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul Benjamin. Former Assistant U.S. Attorney Lawrence Casper contributed significantly to the investigation and prosecution. DEFENDANTS Case Number 20-cr-2054-JO Marco Antonio Lopez-Guerrero                                                         Mexicali, Mexico aka “Chapo” aka “Marcos” aka “Patron del Meloncillo” aka “Marcos NM” SUMMARY OF CHARGES Conspiracy to Import Methamphetamine – Title 21, U.S.C., Sections 952, 960, and 963 Maximum penalty: Mandatory minimum 10 years to life in prison INVESTIGATING AGENCIES Drug Enforcement Administration Homeland Security Investigations Imperial County Sheriff’s Department U.S. Border Patrol – El Centro Sector This investigation is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF San Diego comprises agents and officers from FBI, Homeland Security Investigations, DEA, ATF, U.S. Marshals, Department of Defense, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Naval Criminal Investigative Service, IRS Criminal Investigation, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Customs and Border Protection and Interpol, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California. Contact Kelly Thornton Director of Media Relations U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of California 619.546.9726 Follow us on Twitter @SDCAnews Updated November 12, 2026 Component USAO - California, Southern Press Release Number: CAS26-1112-Lopez-Guerrero

title: Mableton Man Faces Federal Charges After Agents Seize Nearly 60 Pounds of Fentanyl from Backyard Shed
body: Press Release Mableton Man Faces Federal Charges After Agents Seize Nearly 60 Pounds of Fentanyl from Backyard Shed Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Georgia Atlanta – Michael Antonio Cruz was arraigned earlier today in federal court on drug trafficking charges related to the discovery of nearly 60 pounds of fentanyl in a shed behind one of his alleged residences. “The staggering quantity of fentanyl Cruz allegedly possessed posed a critical threat to public health and safety. But for the intervention of law enforcement, the fentanyl could have reached the streets and had potentially fatal consequences,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “My office will continue to work closely with our law enforcement partners to aggressively prosecute the criminals who deal this poison in our community.” “Fentanyl continues to devastate families and communities across this country,” said Michael J. Connolly, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the DEA Atlanta Field Division. “The alleged trafficking of 60 pounds of this deadly substance underscores the magnitude of the threat we face. DEA will continue to pursue those responsible for putting profits over human lives. Our mission remains dedicated to protecting our communities, preventing drug trafficking, and working toward a Fentanyl Free America.” According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the charges, and other information presented in court: On September 30, 2026, federal agents conducting a narcotics investigation executed search warrants at three residences allegedly owned by Cruz. In Austell, Georgia, agents searched a backyard shed and found nearly 60 pounds of fentanyl shaped in 26 individually wrapped bricks with stamped markings on each side. In a Mableton, Georgia residence, agents found multiple scales, buckets of a cutting agent commonly used with methamphetamine and cocaine, plastic bins containing methamphetamine residue, vacuum sealing machines, and vacuum sealing packages. Agents also found a false vent that opened into a void in the wall, where they discovered more than $74,000 in cash. Today, Michael Antonio Cruz, 32, of Mableton, Georgia, was arraigned in federal court on an indictment returned by a grand jury on November 3, 2026, that charged him with conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine and fentanyl as well as possession with intent to distribute fentanyl. Cruz was ordered detained in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service pending further proceedings. Members of the public are reminded that the indictment only contains charges. The defendant is presumed innocent of the charges, and it will be the government’s burden to prove the defendant’s guilt beyond a reasonable doubt at trial. This case is being investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, with valuable assistance provided by the Cobb County Police Department, Cobb County Sheriff’s Office, and Homeland Security Investigations. Assistant United States Attorney Edward C. Robinson Jr. is prosecuting the case. This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. The U.S. Attorney’s Office in Atlanta recommends parents and children learn about the dangers of drugs at the following web site: www.justthinktwice.gov . For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga . title: Pair who led retail theft conspiracy to be arraigned for $5.6 million in theft from four retailers
body: Press Release Pair who led retail theft conspiracy to be arraigned for $5.6 million in theft from four retailers Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Washington Defendants allegedly collected more than $3 million selling stolen goods to consumers, third-party resellers, and wholesalers Seattle – Two men who allegedly led a sophisticated scheme to steal and resell products from four online retailers will be arraigned tomorrow on a three-count indictment that outlined the multi-million-dollar fraud scheme, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Brian Vinh Pham of 29, of Arlington, Texas, and Romar Aragon Noto, 22, of North Hills, California, will be arraigned on the indictment tomorrow at 11:00 AM in U.S. District Court in Seattle. According to the indictment, between April 2023, and February 2026, Pham and Noto led a sophisticated retail theft ring that transported stolen property across the country, including into the Western District of Washington. The men stole the merchandise by exploiting return policies and obtaining fraudulent refunds.  For one retailer, they also exploited a glitch on the retailer’s website to obtain more than 55,000 pieces of merchandise without payment. They then sold the stolen goods directly to consumers, to other third-party resellers, and to wholesalers. The indictment details how Pham and Noto’s group targeted four retailers to obtain more than $3.2 million worth of goods by obtaining fraudulent refunds. After ordering the merchandise, they would initiate returns with retailers who paid refunds when the return shipping labels were scanned.  The theft ring used a variety of tactics to show the return packages were shipped but never actually returned the stolen goods. During a five-month period, a retailer of home improvement goods, Retailer 2, paid $124,000 in refunds to Pham and Noto’s group for over 200 expander tools, only to have the return labels affixed to empty envelopes or boxes. Pham and Noto sold expander tools via Amazon Marketplace for $96,000. Similarly, during a 10-month period, the co-conspirators ordered and obtained more than $162,000 in refunds for more than 350 tankless water heaters that they failed to return. About 297 of the water heaters were sold on Amazon Marketplace for more than $181,000. In total, that victim was defrauded of more than 2,800 items valued at more than $1.4 million. Retailer 3, a clothing retailer, was defrauded of 15,000 pieces of clothing worth over $1 million. The clothes were sold in bulk to other third-party resellers. Retailer 4 was defrauded of clothing worth $767,000 in some 900 orders where a refund was claimed but the goods were not returned.  Retailer 1, a manufacturer of insulated stainless-steel tumblers, issued refunds totaling more than $53,000 for over 1,000 tumblers that were never returned. Pham and Noto’s group also targeted Retailer 1 when its website had a glitch that canceled bulk orders but then still fulfilled and shipped some canceled orders without payment.  The pair’s group used the messaging platform Discord to coordinate placing more than 7,000 orders, seeking to obtain more than 150,000 tumblers valued at about $6.5 million.  The group successfully stole more than 55,000 tumblers worth approximately $2.4 million through 2,700 orders.  Pham and Noto used warehouses in Texas and California to store the enormous inventory before selling the tumblers on Amazon Marketplace, to third-party resellers, and to wholesalers. The co-conspirators set up various business entities and bank accounts to execute their scheme. Both men are charged with money laundering for transferring their ill-gotten proceeds from one of their business accounts to another account. Conspiracy to commit interstate transportation of stolen property is punishable by up to five years in prison. Money laundering is punishable by up to ten years in prison. The charges contained in the indictment are only allegations.  A person is presumed innocent unless and until he or she is proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. The case is being investigated by the FBI. pham_noto_indictment.pdf Contact Press contact for the U.S. Attorney’s Office is Communications Director Emily Langlie at (206) 553-4110 or Emily.Langlie@usdoj.gov . Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Fraud Component USAO - Washington, Western

title: Woman Admits Stealing Cosmetics from Stores in Missouri, Around the Country
body: Press Release Woman Admits Stealing Cosmetics from Stores in Missouri, Around the Country Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Missouri ST. LOUIS – A woman has admitted participating in a nationwide shoplifting spree that cost retailers $188,000. Ionela Chiciu, 19, pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court in St. Louis to one count of interstate transportation of stolen property. She admitted stealing cosmetic products and other merchandise between Jan. 9, 2024, and May 27, 2026, from retailers throughout the United States. Chiciu traveled from California to various states, including Kansas, Missouri and Illinois, to steal. She and others hid the products in their clothing and/or bags and left the stores without paying. One retailer lost $143,805 to the scheme, and other stores lost thousands each time Chiciu and the others visited. On May 23, 2026, Chiciu and an unknown co-conspirator stole about $2,097 worth of cosmetic products from a Prairie Village, Kansas retailer. About an hour later, they took $9,725 worth of cosmetic products from a store in Independence, Missouri. Four days later, they stole nearly $19,000 worth of cosmetic products and other merchandise from five stores in Illinois before driving a car containing the stolen goods to Chesterfield, Missouri, where they were arrested after stealing $13,853 worth of cosmetic products. Chiciu and her co-conspirators stole a total of about $188,473 worth of merchandise. Chiciu, who is also known as Ionela Chiciu-Nistor, Ionela Nistor Chiciu, Ionela Aurora Chiciu and Aurora Nistor, has used different home addresses during her arrests. U.S. Immigrations and Customs Enforcement’s Homeland Security Investigations, the Chesterfield Police Department and police departments around the country investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Karin Schute is prosecuting the case. Contact Robert Patrick, Public Affairs Officer, robert.patrick@usdoj.gov. Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - Missouri, Eastern

title: Coralville Man Sentenced to Over 11 Years in Federal Prison for Firearm and Receipt of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Coralville Man Sentenced to Over 11 Years in Federal Prison for Firearm and Receipt of Child Pornography Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Iowa DAVENPORT, Iowa – A Coralville, Iowa man was sentenced on November 12, 2026, to 140 months in federal prison for two counts of possession of an unregistered firearm and one count of receipt of child pornography. According to public court documents and evidence presented at sentencing, Edward Ian Whitehouse, also known as Kodi, 59, received numerous images and videos containing child sexual abuse material, including content with minors as young as infancy. Whitehouse messaged self-purported minors and made plans for the self-purported minors to travel to Iowa to meet with him and engaged in sex acts. Whitehouse was found to be in possession of numerous weapons and ammunition, including four rifles, two shotguns, two handguns, 15 different firearm magazines, an AR-15 rifle with a silencer attached, and a separate a rifle silencer. Neither silencer was registered to Whitehouse under the National Firearms Registration and Transfer Record. After completing his term of imprisonment, Whitehouse will be required to serve an eight-year term of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. Whitehouse was also ordered to pay $12,000 in restitution. United States Attorney David C. Waterman of the Southern District of Iowa made the announcement. The Coralville Police Department, Joint Forensic Analysis Cyber Team, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives investigated the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. For more information about Project Safe Neighborhoods, please visit Justice.gov/PSN. Contact MacKenzie Tubbs Public Information Officer 515-473-9300 USAIAS.PAO@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Topics Project Safe Childhood Project Safe Neighborhoods Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Iowa, Southern

title: Florida Man Sentenced for Stealing Millions of Dollars from Lenders Using Sham Cosmetic Surgery Clinics and Stolen Identities
body: Press Release Florida Man Sentenced for Stealing Millions of Dollars from Lenders Using Sham Cosmetic Surgery Clinics and Stolen Identities Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Today, A Wellington, Florida, man was sentenced today to 84 months in prison for using sham cosmetic surgery clinics and the stolen identities of more than 100 people to defraud medical lenders of approximately $2.3 million, and for fraudulently seeking COVID-19 disaster relief loans. “Jacquez Tullis built fake medical clinics using stolen identities, including those of practicing doctors and deceased individuals, and used them to steal millions from lenders,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “When the pandemic hit, Tullis then tried to exploit taxpayer-funded relief meant for struggling small businesses. Today’s sentence makes clear that the Fraud Division will hold accountable those who abuse the public’s trust, whether they steal from private lenders or from the American people.” “The defendant’s actions represent a serious breach of trust, exploiting the identities of innocent individuals and manipulating financial institutions for personal gain,” said Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of FBI Miami. “Fraud schemes of this magnitude undermine the integrity of our financial system and inflict real harm on victims whose identities are stolen and misused. The FBI remains committed to protecting the American public, holding accountable those who exploit others for financial gain, and pursuing those who believe they can hide behind elaborate schemes.” According to court documents and admissions in his plea, from approximately April 2018 through February 2024, Jaquez Tullis, 42, and his co-conspirators created six sham medical clinics that claimed to offer cosmetic surgery and other medical services, but provided no real care.  The conspirators registered the clinics with the Florida Department of State using stolen personal identifying information of practicing doctors and others without their knowledge or consent.  In some cases, they listed those doctors as clinic owners on applications to become approved merchants with six medical lenders.  Those lenders, two FDIC-insured banks and four financial technology companies financed out-of-pocket procedures not covered by insurance. Once the clinics were approved, the conspirators submitted fraudulent credit card applications to the lenders in the names of more than 100 individuals, seeking approximately $3.1 million.  The applications falsely represented that the funds were for cosmetic surgery and other services the clinics would provide.  In fact, the individuals did not know about or authorize the applications and did not need or want any treatment. According to death records, some had died before the dates they supposedly received care. Separately, from April through August 2020, Tullis submitted at least nine fraudulent applications on behalf of certain businesses to the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) for Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) loans, a federal stimulus program authorized as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act.  Tullis obtained funds under EIDL program by submitting false and fraudulent loan applications that collectively sought $696,860 in EIDL funds. The loan applications falsely represented, among other things, the business’ number of employees and revenue. Tullis pleaded guilty on July 21, 2026, to conspiracy to commit bank fraud and aggravated identity theft. U.S. District Judge Rodolfo A. Ruiz, II, of the Southern District of Florida sentenced Jacquez Dion Tullis, to 60 months on the bank fraud conspiracy count and a consecutive 24 months on the aggravated identity theft count, for a total of 84 months in prison, to be followed by 5 years of supervised release. Tullis was also ordered to pay $2,309,859.44 in restitution, $200 in special assessment, and forfeiture money judgement of $2,309,859.44 Two co-defendants were previously sentenced: Taneika Nakia Pace, 50, of Hallandale Beach, was the manager two of the sham clinics. Pace pleaded guilty to bank fraud on June 15, 2026, and was sentenced on September 2, 2026, to six months in prison and four years of supervised release. She was ordered to pay $49,825 in restitution and to forfeit $23,200. Junaque Nicole Tullis, also known as “Juanaque Tullis,” 46, of Coral Springs, submitted at least five fraudulent EIDL applications to the SBA between April and December 2020, seeking approximately $164,521 in the names of several businesses and herself. The applications contained false statements about the number of employees and revenue of the businesses.  Junaque Tullis pleaded guilty to wire fraud on April 23, 2026, and was sentenced on August 13, 2026, to eight months in prison and three years of supervised release.  She was ordered to pay $4,000 in restitution and to forfeit $4,000. All three defendants were charged as part of the Justice Department’s 2025 National Health Care Fraud Takedown, announced on June 30, 2025. FBI investigated the case. Trial Attorney Shana Priore of the Fraud Division’s Public Trust and Financial Integrity Section prosecuted the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Sandra Demirci of the Southern District of Florida handled asset forfeiture. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1357
