While voice assistants have long been great for quick tasks like playing a playlist or getting directions home, all that quiet time on the road is also an opportunity to catch up, prepare for what’s ahead, or simply think out loud. Following our rollout on Android Auto and cars with Google built-in , today we’re bringing the Gemini app directly to Apple CarPlay. Now, iOS users can have natural, free-flowing conversations with Gemini Live right from their car’s display — hands-free, so you can get more done while keeping your hands on the wheel and your eyes on the road. Pick up where you left off — or start a fresh conversation We designed Gemini on CarPlay to work like a conversational driving companion that minimizes distraction. When you tap the Gemini app icon on your CarPlay screen or side rail, you can easily pick up where you left off with a recent chat or start a fresh conversation. You can talk back and forth with Gemini at your own pace — interrupting to add a detail, changing the subject, or pausing when you need to focus on an exit. Make the most of your drive Whether you’re commuting or setting out on a road trip, Gemini on CarPlay helps you be more productive during your ride. Here are a few ways to make the most of your drive: Get ready for the day ahead: Use your morning commute to see what's coming up and walk into your first meeting prepared. Ask Gemini what's on your calendar, when you need to leave for your next appointment, or talk through what you want to say before you arrive. Try saying: "What does my day look like?" or "Help me prep for my 10am with the design team." Talk through your inbox: Because Gemini connects with your Google Workspace apps like Gmail and Google Calendar, you can ask for your daily brief 1 , catch up on unread emails, get quick summaries of long email threads, and talk through a quick reply using just your voice. Try saying: “Give me my daily brief for today,” or “Catch me up on my unread emails and summarize Sarah’s Q4 budget thread.” Explore local spots and landmarks: Ask Gemini for recommendations in the area you’re heading to, from a quick place to grab lunch to the backstory on a local landmark. Try saying: “What’s a quick lunch spot in downtown Austin that’s easy to get in and out of?” Brainstorm, rehearse, and learn out loud: A quiet car cabin is one of the best places to think out loud. Use Gemini Live as a sounding board to practice an upcoming presentation, prepare for a tough conversation, or break down a complex topic you’ve been curious about. Try saying: “Let’s roleplay my Q4 pitch — act as a skeptical VP and challenge my strategy,” or “Break down how solid-state EV batteries work in simple terms.” And because your CarPlay conversations sync automatically with the Gemini app on your iPhone, every summary, note, and brainstorm is waiting in your chat history the moment you park. Get started today Gemini on Apple CarPlay is rolling out globally starting today to all Gemini users on iOS across every supported Gemini Live language. To get started, make sure you’ve updated to the latest version of the Gemini app on your iPhone, enabled microphone permissions, and used Gemini Live on your phone at least once. title: Google’s ongoing commitment to the veteran community
body: Google’s ongoing commitment to the veteran community Nov 11, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Google invests in career pathways and grassroots support to help veterans and military spouses successfully transition and thrive at every stage of their civilian lives. Michael Reeves Global co-lead, Google Veterans Network, Employee Resource Group Ronnie Ryder Global co-lead, Google Veterans Network, Employee Resource Group Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary Michael Reeves and Ronnie Ryder share how Google supports veterans through career training and community partnerships. Our Google Launchpad for Veterans program provides service members with cloud and generative AI skill training. We offer no-cost scholarships and digital certificates to help veterans and military spouses find civilian jobs. Google.org supports organizations that help veterans build long-term careers in skilled trades and technical fields. Our teams use AI and 3D technology to connect deployed service members with their families globally. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. As co-leads of the Google Veterans Network (VetNet) Employee Resource Group, we see daily how veterans’ skills translate into high-impact workforce leadership. Through deep collaborations with global non-profits, industry partners, and our own product teams, Google is continuing to invest in career pathways and grassroots support to help veterans and military spouses successfully transition and thrive at every stage of their civilian lives. Expanding skills and career pathways A central part of our efforts is providing veterans with career resources and trainings in the latest tech skills. Here’s what we’re doing: Google Launchpad for Veterans : Now in its third year, this program helps active-duty personnel, transitioning service members, and veterans build practical cloud and generative AI skills, preparing them for credentials like the Generative AI Leader certification. Certifications — available at no cost through this program — are known to help open up career opportunities. In fact, 92% of Google Skills learners say Google Cloud credentials (certifications, skill badges) help them get in-demand jobs faster. 1 Veterans Career Week : Hosted alongside Grow with Google, our flagship initiative expanded internationally this year programming across the U.S., Europe, and Asia-Pacific, reaching over 6,000 participants. At our hands-on Grow with Google workshops, veterans and military families used tools like Career Dreamer, which translates their military experience into civilian resumes. They also received no-cost scholarships for digital and AI training, including the Google AI Professional Certificate . Today, one in ten Google Career Certificate graduates comes from the military community. National Veterans Small Business Week : Grow with Google teamed up with American Corporate Partners (ACP) and Blue Star Families to deliver hands-on AI training during our third annual National Veterans Small Business Week livestream. Attendees learned practical AI skills and gained insights from a veteran-owned small business. Skilled Trades Initiative : Google.org is supporting Hiring Our Heroes, Home Builders Institute, and Student Veterans of America to help 25,000 veterans and military family members build long-term careers in skilled trades. This builds upon prior funding to support student veterans nationwide with broad career readiness programming, including access to Google Career Certificates and Google AI Professional Certificate. Public Sector Enablement : Working alongside partners like Carahsoft, Google Cloud has trained more than 40,000 public sector personnel, including active duty service members and reservists, equipping our military with the hands-on expertise to safely architect what’s next. Investing in community organizations This year’s Google Veteran Impact Awards delivered $500,000 in new funding across four high-impact organizations. Nominated by VetNet Googlers with deep personal ties to their work, these nonprofits represent the groups our veteran community trusts, champions, and volunteers for: FourBlock : Leads employer-hosted transition programs, taught directly by corporate leaders at active workplaces, for veterans to build direct networks and translate their military experience using an AI-enabled platform. Blue Star Families : Serves as the nation’s largest military and veteran family support organization, strengthening families through trusted resources, community partnerships, and scam-prevention education. The Von Terra Project : Empowers veterans transitioning to advanced technical careers through offerings like its comprehensive cybersecurity certification program, which features learning resources, fully funded exam vouchers, and one-on-one industry mentorship. The Job Forum : Facilitates volunteer-led advising where experienced executives and hiring professionals help veterans and spouses translate skills and prepare for interviews. Spotlighting veterans through our products Across Google's products and platforms, we are celebrating and connecting the military community: Google Beam and USO: In partnership with the USO, we’re expanding HP Dimension with Google Beam to 20 locations globally. Powered by AI and 3D technology, Beam provides true-to-life video communication that lets deployed service members and their families feel like they are stepping into the same space. Watch our docuseries connecting four soldiers in Poland with their families in Texas; goo.gle/uso-beam Google Doodle: Our annual Veterans Day Doodle recognizes service, dedication, and courage with the achievement medals representing the six branches of service. These merit-based awards, which honor exceptional teamwork or technical achievements, often represent a junior officer’s, warrant officer’s, or enlisted service member's first individual award for superior performance of their duties and are an important point of pride in veteran life. Camaraderie and purpose don’t end when service members hang up their uniforms. For the thousands of military families transitioning to civilian life each year, that shared sense of mission endures — and at Google, we recognize that the resilience, adaptability, and teamwork forged in service are invaluable assets to our teams. To our veterans, service members, and military families: thank you for your service and leadership. title: Try Tabletop: Customizable, collaborative spaces for groups to plan, play and do more together.
body: Try Tabletop: Customizable, collaborative spaces for groups to plan, play and do more together. Roman Nurik Design & Engineering Lead, Google Labs Nov 11, 2026 Whether you’re planning a family trip, running a rec league or hosting a potluck, coordinating as a group is easier when everyone can pitch in, build and decide together in one place. Today, we’re introducing Tabletop , a new Google Labs experiment built for real-time collaboration. Just add in your links, files, and ideas, then prompt @tabletop — or pick a starter template — to generate custom interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters, and tournament brackets. Once your space is ready, drop the invite link in your group chat to let everyone jump in and use it at the same time, like in a Google Doc. Tabletop is rolling out in the U.S. (18+) via waitlist. Pull up a chair and sign up at labs.google/tabletop .

title: Albany Man Sentenced to 120 Months for Receiving Child Pornography
body: Press Release Albany Man Sentenced to 120 Months for Receiving Child Pornography Wednesday, November 11, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov On November 10, 2026, Gregory Conrad Puzio, a/k/a “Tony G.,” age 41, of Albany, New York, was sentenced to 120 months’ imprisonment for receiving child pornography.  First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III; Anthony Patrone, Special Agent in Charge of the Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI); and New York State Police (NYSP) Superintendent Steven G. James made the announcement. As part of his previously entered guilty plea, Puzio admitted that in February 2025, he used a messaging application to receive child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including a video where a child victim was sexually abused and beaten.  In late June 2025, Puzio was charged by local authorities with use of a child in a sexual performance and possessing a sexual performance by a child based on this conduct but was subsequently released on bond.  After a federal complaint was filed on July 8, 2025, federal agents arrested Puzio and he did not contest federal detention. First Assistant United States Attorney Sarcone stated: “Puzio traded in grotesque videos of children being sexually abused and viciously beaten.  After he was released by a New York State court, my office and our partners took immediate action to make sure that this child predator would not be back in the community to engage in further crimes against the most vulnerable among us. This administration shall continue to act swiftly to protect the citizens of the Northern District of New York when the state, with its failed policies when it comes to protecting its citizens from dangerous criminals such as Puzio, allows them to come back into the community pending adjudication.” HSI Special Agent in Charge Patrone stated: “The abuse depicted in the material Gregory Puzio received is profoundly disturbing, and children deserve to be protected from those who perpetuate this exploitation. This 120-month sentence reflects the serious consequences for such conduct and the resolve of HSI and our partners to identify offenders, support victims, and safeguard children. I thank HSI Albany, the New York State Police, the U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General, and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for their determined work on this investigation and prosecution.” New York State Police Superintendent Steven G. James said, “Behind every image of child sexual abuse is a real child who has suffered unimaginable harm. This sentence holds Gregory Puzio accountable for his role in perpetuating that abuse. I commend our investigators and federal partners for their work on this case and their continued commitment to protecting children and bringing those who exploit them to justice.” U.S. District Judge Mae A. D’Agostino also imposed a 15-year term of supervised release to follow Puzio’s release from prison.  As part of his plea agreement, Puzio agreed to forfeit the phone he used to receive child pornography. This case was investigated by HSI and the NYSP, with assistance from the United States Postal Service’s Office of Inspector General.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Joshua R. Rosenthal prosecuted this case as part of Project Safe Childhood. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated November 11, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: Experience the art and legacy of Dr. Esther Mahlangu
body: Experience the art and legacy of Dr. Esther Mahlangu Nov 11, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Discover Google Arts & Culture's online retrospective of the South African artist, which features more than 45 curated stories, virtual tours, and her early memories brought to life with AI. Dr Nontobeko Ntombela Senior Lecturer, Department of Curatorial, Public and Visual Cultures, Wits School of Arts, University of the Witwatersrand Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary Dr. Nontobeko Ntombela presents the first online retrospective of artist Dr. Esther Mahlangu on Google Arts & Culture to honor her 91st birthday. This collection features over 45 stories, archival materials, and AI-generated recreations of her early life to preserve Ndebele heritage for a global audience. You can explore the full exhibition and learn more about her artistic legacy by visiting the Google Arts & Culture website. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Dr. Nontobeko Ntombela presents the first online retrospective of artist Dr. Esther Mahlangu on Google Arts & Culture. You can explore over 45 stories, rare archival materials, and murals documenting her life and artistic legacy. We used artificial intelligence to recreate undocumented memories from her early years before her first recorded works. This project preserves Ndebele culture by combining historical research with new video technology for a global audience. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. We are celebrating artist Dr. Esther Mahlangu with a new online retrospective on Google Arts & Culture. Because some of her early history was missing, we used artificial intelligence to recreate her childhood memories based on her own stories. You can now explore over 45 exhibitions, view her murals, and learn about Ndebele culture from anywhere in the world. This project preserves her artistic legacy for you and future generations to enjoy. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Today we’re sharing the first online retrospective of artist Dr. Esther Mahlangu on Google Arts & Culture, honoring her pioneering spirit on her 91st birthday. More than 45 stories and a rich archive covering her art , life , and legacy are now accessible to a global audience. For many years, I have worked closely with Esther and her family. It’s a relationship built on years of research and a deep admiration for her as both an artist and a person. It was out of this long-standing connection that the vision for “‘ Then I Knew I Was Good at Painting’: Esther Mahlangu, a Retrospective ,” was born. My goal has always been to present a comprehensive exploration of her life and work, contributing to my long-standing research on South African women artists who have made an impact on the arts since the early 20th century. Through my research, I gathered a rich collection of her work, including large-scale murals , intimate pieces , and rare archival materials . But the archives didn’t include anything from her life before 1980, so crucial pieces of her history were missing. This void challenged us to find new ways to tell her full story. A collaboration session with Esther Mahlangu, Nontobeko Ntombela, and the Google team. In collaboration with Google Arts & Culture, we used AI to visually recreate Esther’s undocumented memories . The process brought us closer to her work and prompted further recollections from Esther herself. This project brought our curatorial and archival work together with the technical expertise of Google DeepMind and Google Arts & Culture Lab, alongside research and design studio Domestic Data Streamers’ synthetic memories initiative. Through a series of workshops and interviews , we were able to document a missing period of Mam' Esther's history, from when she started painting at age 10 until her first documented works in 1980. These stories — such as the moment she discovered her talent for painting as a 10-year-old using feathers instead of a brush — became the source material for our work. Following the methodology from the synthetic memories initiative and using archival material, the team generated still images based on Esther’s memories. They then used Veo to turn the images into videos that brought Esther's early days to life. The stories also contribute to the online archive of Esther’s life on Google Arts & Culture. More than 45 exhibitions , curated in collaboration with Art of Contemporary Africa, Iziko Museums of South Africa, the British Museum, the Jean Pigozzi Collection, the National Museum of Women in the Arts, and Serpentine, tell the story of how she came to be known in the world, through her artwork , archives, Street View , and more. Portrait of Esther Mahlangu taken at Botshabelo, c. 1980-1991; Art of Contemporary Africa | Source Esther Mahlangu: Untitled, 2014; Art of Contemporary Africa | Source The Esther Mahlangu Art Studio at the Esther Mahlangu Homestead, 2025; Art of Contemporary Africa | Source Installation of the Esther Mahlangu retrospective at Iziko South African National Gallery, 2024; Art of Contemporary Africa | Source Esther Mahlangu: Ndebele Abstract, 2019; Art of Contemporary Africa, courtesy of the Larry Warsh Collection | Source This project demonstrates a new way to approach the preservation of cultural heritage, with technology that’s guided at every step by a respect for personal memory and historical accuracy. It is my hope that this retrospective cements Esther’s place as a pivotal voice in global contemporary art, invites audiences to reimagine the possibilities of her archive, and ensures her story and her artistic vision can inspire generations to come. title: Bowman, The U.S. Economy and Considerations for Monetary Policy
body:

Main Menu Toggle Button Sections Search Toggle Button Search Search Submit Button Submit Home News & Events Speeches Speech PDF November 10, 2026 The U.S. Economy and Considerations for Monetary Policy Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle W. Bowman At the C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics Council on Foreign Relations, Washington, D.C. Share Watch Live Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman presented identical remarks at a subsequent event held by Unleash Prosperity Now on the same day. Good afternoon. It is a pleasure to join you today at the Council on Foreign Relations to discuss my outlook for the U.S. economy. 1 Economic growth has gained momentum this year, driven by robust investment demand and solid consumer spending, and the labor market now appears to have stabilized. These outcomes suggest that the policy rate cuts toward the end of last year helped to address some labor market weakness. We are experiencing rapid technological change and ongoing geopolitical tensions, while inflation pressures have persisted for longer than I had hoped and have shown recent signs of broadening. Despite these challenges, increased investment in and use of artificial intelligence (AI), or super intelligence, are boosting economic growth and productivity and American families appear to be resilient. The Federal Reserve's monetary policy goals are to achieve maximum employment and price stability. While the labor market has improved more than I expected this year, our progress on lowering inflation has disappointed. Therefore, bringing inflation down remains a priority. I am also monitoring expectations about AI and energy prices, and how they influence the risks to achieving our mandates. Consistent with my views following our September FOMC meeting, I continue to focus on interpreting the underlying trends in the economy and the evolution of financial conditions. 2 In my remarks today, I will review our most recent FOMC policy meeting and discuss current economic conditions and my near-term outlook for the economy. I will then turn to recent developments in energy markets and the AI buildout and will conclude with my thoughts on the appropriate path of monetary policy. Update on the Most Recent FOMC Meeting At last month's FOMC meeting, I joined my colleagues to support holding the federal funds rate target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent. This approach was consistent with my view that further changes in the policy rate should wait until we had a better understanding of how conditions would evolve and how the recent rate increase would influence the underlying trends in the economy. Maintaining the policy stance at the October meeting allowed us to assess the incoming data. While I continue to expect that several of the factors currently boosting inflation will abate next year, currently inflation has proven to be more persistent than I had anticipated. It is also important to gain greater clarity on the effect of recent market volatility on financial conditions. Economic and Financial Conditions U.S. economic growth has stepped up this year. After rising a solid 2.4 percent during the first half of the year, real gross domestic product (GDP) likely increased at an even stronger pace of more than 3 percent in the third quarter, well above last year's 2 percent pace. 3 Economic growth has been supported by robust increases in AI-related capital expenditures and solid consumer spending. However, some interest-rate-sensitive sectors like residential investment have declined, and the recent rise in mortgage rates appears to be dragging home construction and sales down further. Consumer spending has strengthened this year, despite softness in real incomes and declining sentiment, which are partly due to higher energy prices. Labor Market Conditions Labor market conditions look to have improved since last year. Over the course of this year, the unemployment rate has edged down to 4.1 percent in October, remaining close to my estimate of its natural rate. Job gains have been above last year's anemic pace, averaging about 80,000 per month through October, and have broadened across industries beyond health care and social assistance. The labor market continues to show low dynamism, with low-hiring and low-firing conditions as we sometimes see in a late-cycle expansion. The job-finding rate has been low, especially for new labor force entrants, and the share of long-term unemployed workers has moved up significantly. Workers' perceptions of job availability in the Conference Board survey have remained soft in recent months. On their own, these data would be consistent with a higher unemployment rate than currently reported. However, layoffs have moved down this year, offsetting the softness in hiring. In plain terms, workers are both less likely to find a new job and less likely to be laid off, a somewhat unusual pattern. Although stable, the labor market does not appear to be tight, as wage growth has slowed to a modest pace. On a 12-month basis, the wages and salaries component of the employment cost index increased 3.1 percent in September, the same pace as the change in average hourly earnings for October. Both measures have slowed noticeably from a year ago. An increasing number of workers have taken on a supplemental part-time job to make ends meet, as the share of multiple job holders has increased back to levels seen in early 2025. Given strong productivity gains in recent years, wage growth at this pace is in line with or even below the pace we would expect if inflation was running at 2 percent. Inflation Progress on lowering inflation has stalled over the past two years or so. Today's consumer price index suggests that 12-month core PCE inflation likely moved up further to 3.3 percent in October, as upward pressures from higher energy prices and AI-related demand continue to flow through to core goods and services prices. Lack of progress on lowering inflation largely reflects a confluence of shocks unrelated to conditions in the labor market. Tariffs, energy, and AI-related price pressures each accounted for roughly one-fourth of above-target core PCE inflation over the 12 months ending in September. The remaining one-fourth likely reflects persistent effects from the inflationary shocks in recent years. Price pressures had been concentrated in a few categories, but the latest data suggest that these pressures may be broadening. It is important to ensure that those inflationary pressures do not intensify, further broaden, or become embedded in consumer and business expectations. But today's consumer price index data suggest that inflation pressures may persist for longer. Tariff effects should further wane going forward. Energy-related price pressures should unwind when the Middle East conflict resolves. And inflation pressures related to the AI buildout seem to persist despite some early signs of slowing. I mostly view these pressures as reflecting relative price shocks in specific sectors of the economy. For example, the AI buildout has quickly shifted investment demand toward specific types of high-tech capital, putting upward pressure on prices due to relatively inelastic supply in the near term. As these shocks wane or unwind and with no inflationary pressures emerging in the labor market, my forecast is for core PCE inflation to move closer to 2 percent next year. Financial Conditions Financial conditions have tightened a bit recently because of lower equity prices, higher private interest rates, and a stronger dollar. That tightening comes against a backdrop of increased market volatility. Corporate bond and mortgage rate spreads have widened, and equity valuations in the tech sector have dropped, as investors appear to be reassessing expected returns and the risks associated with increased external financing for AI investment projects. Economic Outlook and Risks Looking ahead, my expectation is that policies designed to boost the economic potential of the U.S. economy would continue to support productivity, growth, and business confidence. These policies include pragmatic regulations, lower taxes, and more supportive policies toward businesses. I expect the labor market to remain stable and inflation to slow, as special factors currently holding inflation elevated gradually wane or unwind next year. Over time, I also expect increased AI adoption to raise productivity and put some downward pressure on inflation as lower production costs are passed through to consumer prices. On risks to the outlook, with the labor market improving since last year, I am more attentive to the inflation side of our mandate. Sustained supply-chain pressures from the AI buildout or greater pass-through of higher energy costs could cause inflation pressures to persist. I can also envision a scenario in which the effects of the Middle East conflict and the tech investment boom wane or unwind quickly. In this scenario, I would also expect a timelier return of core PCE inflation toward our target. I also see a number of risks to the outlook for economic activity, many originating in financial markets. These risks include a large correction in equity valuations, if returns on AI investment fall short of expectations, and a sharp increase in private longer-term interest rates. Lower equity prices could undermine the resilience in consumer spending. And higher interest rates could further strain interest-rate-sensitive sectors of the economy, like housing and small business investment. I will continue to closely monitor developments in credit and equity markets to assess risks to economic growth and financial stability. Important Issues for Monetary Policy I see conditions in energy markets and the AI buildout as two important issues for the economy in the months ahead. Developments in these two areas could have material effects on both sides of our mandate and could influence my views on the path for monetary policy. Energy Markets The Middle East conflict has disrupted energy markets, impairing the flow of oil and other commodities passing through the Strait of Hormuz, which accounted for about 20 percent of global oil supply before the conflict—roughly equivalent to total U.S. oil consumption. As tensions rose, Brent oil prices moved up to and above $110 per barrel in the second half of October before dropping sharply last week on optimism that an agreement between the U.S. and Iran could be reached following the midterm elections. Although crude oil flows in the Persian Gulf have recovered to near pre-conflict levels in recent weeks, freight rates and insurance premiums have surged because of more complex logistics and ongoing geopolitical risk, raising the cost of delivered oil to many markets around the world. Prices for gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel also moved up to near or even above their highs in the spring. These higher prices reflected both higher crude oil prices and wider refining margins, as refineries in both the Persian Gulf and Russia have been damaged as a result of ongoing military conflicts in both regions. Prices for refined products have retraced some of the earlier gains more recently as crude oil prices have receded and margins have shown signs of normalizing. While the outcomes of these conflicts remain uncertain, my approach is to look through temporary energy-driven inflation, when possible, and to remain alert to signs that it is spreading into broader prices or expectations. If geopolitical tensions persist, energy prices may stay elevated in the near term, increasing risks that core inflation may also stay elevated because of increased pass-through to consumer prices of higher production and transportation costs. Although the U.S. economy is now a net exporter of oil products and less energy intensive, we could still see an impact on economic activity from higher energy prices. The recent deterioration in consumer sentiment measures suggests households may be internalizing a more persistent reduction in their purchasing power. I would be especially concerned about effects on both sides of our mandate if there were further significant disruptions to energy markets. An escalation of geopolitical tensions could have more meaningful effects on real activity because of higher uncertainty and the larger impact of energy prices on lower- and middle-income consumers. Even with a quick resolution to the Middle East conflict, it may take some time for energy prices to normalize. Futures markets expect oil prices to decline only gradually, as global oil consumption is projected to exceed supply at least through the end of this year. As inventories have been drawn down, the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) has reached a bit less than 50 days of crude oil imports, the lowest level since the early 1980s, reflecting both this year's and the larger 2022 SPR releases. A number of new Gulf pipelines to bypass the Strait of Hormuz are under construction or expansion, with the United Arab Emirates' West–East expansion coming online in early 2027 and most others in 2028 and beyond. Domestic oil production could also continue to rise, which would put downward pressure on fuel costs. AI Buildout In remarks earlier this year, I discussed the responsible use of AI in the financial system. 4 Today I will describe how this technology is shaping the broader economy. Given the transformative promise of this technology, investment in data centers has boomed and has been a major influence on the U.S. economy. With plans for new data centers continuing to surge, I expect the AI shock to play out over some time. However, as these investments are increasingly being financed with external funds, including off-balance-sheet liabilities, I am also focused on potential risks to the economy and financial stability if revenues from AI customers disappoint. We may still be in the early days when investment rises rapidly while workers and firms determine the best use cases before we see more meaningful effects on productivity. The boom in data center investment is undeniable, with growth in real business fixed investment strengthening further this year to a pace like the 1990s tech boom. High-tech equipment, software, and data center construction have accounted for the large majority of growth in business investment since 2025, with gains broadening to other categories this year. AI adoption has grown significantly, especially among larger firms, with about 25 percent of businesses and roughly 10 percent of workers reporting using AI every day in their work. However, use varies greatly across industries and occupations, with stronger adoption in information and other business services sectors. I think there is a risk that some workers will be displaced as firms adopt this technology, even as others see their productivity—and wages—rise. Monetary policy cannot address that transition directly, but it should support a dynamic labor market that facilitates the necessary retraining and mobility of workers across jobs. AI revenues have been rising quickly but are not yet sufficient to pay for the expense of maintaining existing and developing new AI models and data centers. As capital spending has surged, hyperscalers and other companies have increasingly been sourcing funds from credit and equity markets. And as investors see an increased risk in these investments, the cost of financing has been rising notably. In addition to financing costs, the AI buildout is also putting upward pressure on a number of price categories. Prices of memory chips, semiconductors, computers, and other electronic products have increased sharply this year—in a few categories by double digits—as demand from data centers has outpaced supply. I expect production capacity to catch up to demand gradually over time. AI-related debt has been rising rapidly, with notable gains in corporate bonds, private credit, and project finance, and is on track to exceed $800 billion this year. Other obligations, in the form of long-term lease and contract commitments and residual value guarantees, have also surged and their potential payments are estimated at more than three times the amount of debt. Given their strong credit ratings, hyperscalers and large tech firms have assumed off-balance-sheet liabilities to allow smaller and riskier companies to use them as collateral in asset-based financing for data center construction and the purchase of accelerated computing equipment. These connections among AI firms have also been accompanied by hyperscalers and chip designers making equity investments in smaller companies that purchase their products, creating the appearance of circular financing. The largest U.S. bank holding companies have some exposure to AI-related financing, which is scrutinized during annual supervisory stress tests. Life insurance companies, pension funds, private credit, and mutual funds also have exposure. Most of these entities are well capitalized and have stable funding. But the complex nature of the financing structures makes it difficult to properly assess counterparty risk. Risks seem to be concentrated in only a few large firms that provide AI services, including AI labs and the hyperscalers. If AI-related revenues fall short of sharply rising costs, especially as public sentiment and local opposition could lead to increased regulation and delays, we could see a sharp correction in equity prices for AI firms, higher financing costs, and reduced access to credit. This shock would likely slow the AI buildout and soften both economic activity and inflation. We may have already seen some reassessment of expected returns play out in recent weeks as equity valuations dropped, corporate bond spreads widened, and credit default swaps increased for some companies involved in the AI buildout. I will be looking at how momentum in adoption of and investment in this technology evolves and for possible effects on both inflation and employment. The Path Forward for Monetary Policy As we think about the path ahead, it is important to remember that over the past two years the U.S. economy has experienced successive inflationary shocks that have not been driven by labor market conditions. Monetary policy cannot offset the direct effects of tariffs and energy costs on inflation, but it plays a central role in containing the second-round effects. Monetary policy also has limited influence on AI-related price pressures. However, in certain segments of AI-intensive sectors, particularly among newer and medium-sized firms, higher interest rates appear to be holding back investment and purchasing decisions. As I noted earlier, financial conditions have tightened. Against this backdrop, the benefit of additional policy tightening has to be carefully weighed against its costs for interest-rate-sensitive sectors. The October Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey on Bank Lending Practices (SLOOS) suggests that the concentration of demand weakness in real estate loan categories reflects existing headwinds in those sectors. 5 Time will help us learn more about the durability of momentum in AI-related demand and the evolution of geopolitical risks, both of which could be critical in the months ahead for setting our policy stance. Greater clarity on AI-related financing conditions and the sustainability of AI investments should increase my confidence in future policy decisions. Geopolitical conditions affect commodity markets and the degree of economic uncertainty perceived by households and businesses. Before our next meeting in December, we will receive the PCE inflation report for October and the employment report for November. Today, I am seeing signs that inflation pressures are persisting, while labor market conditions appear to be firming. This indicates that there is still work to do to bring inflation closer to 2 percent. Given the recent market volatility, I will also continue to closely monitor how developments in financial conditions influence the economic outlook. In the meantime, I will continue to meet with a broad range of contacts to inform my assessment of economic conditions and the appropriate stance of policy. It is important to remember that monetary policy is not on a preset course. At each FOMC meeting, my colleagues and I will evaluate incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the implications for the risks to our dual-mandate goals of maximum employment and price stability. Thank you again for the invitation to join you this afternoon. I look forward to our discussion. 1. The views expressed here are my own and are not necessarily those of my colleagues on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) or the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Return to text 2. See Atlantic Council (2026), "Federal Reserve Vice Chair Michelle Bowman on Modernizing Financial Regulation," AC Front Page event, Washington, October 1. Return to text 3. Note that currently reported GDP growth in the first half of this year may be overestimated by about 0.3 percentage point, reflecting downward revisions in the retail sales annual update that were not folded into the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) 2026 annual revision of the national accounts. Return to text 4. See Michelle W. title: Pixel 10 with Gemini Intelligence, custom widgets, and more in our November Pixel Drop
body: Pixel 10 with Gemini Intelligence, custom widgets, and more in our November Pixel Drop Nov 10, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Explore the latest Pixel features, including Gemini Intelligence updates and the launch of Pixel Tag. Mayra Fajardo Product Marketing Manager Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Our November Pixel Drop is here, with new and expanded features making your Pixel devices more personalized, intuitive, and handy. See how we’re bringing smarter automation, next-level personalization, and upgraded connectivity to your favorite devices. Updates start rolling out today and will continue over the next several weeks. Use Pixel 10 with Gemini Intelligence Gemini Intelligence is now available on Pixel 10 devices , bringing new capabilities like Rambler, personalized suggestions, and taking care of multi-step tasks — like placing your morning coffee order. Polish your messages with Rambler on Pixel 10: Voice typing just got a major upgrade. Rambler can automatically remove filler words like “um,” and format your thoughts into clear, polished text. Just speak naturally, review, and send. Complete multi-step tasks with Gemini: Whether you’re getting groceries, booking a ride, ordering takeout, or trying to find a reservation at your favorite restaurant, let Gemini handle the logistics so you can focus on other tasks. Now available in Japan, UK, and India. Receive proactive suggestions: From sharing your ETA with a tap when someone asks when you’ll arrive, to helping you find the perfect dinner spot, your Pixel anticipates what you need with timely information and suggested actions, so you can accomplish your daily tasks faster. 1 Also, coming soon to Pixel Watch 4. Create more personalized widgets: Ever find yourself wanting a widget that doesn’t seem to exist? Create personalized widgets, like a tracker to follow your monthly spending, a game day widget with your team colors, or a getaway countdown that automatically pulls in flight and reservation details. Your home screen can be as personalized as you want it to be. Also, coming soon to Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5. 2 Catch up on long conversations: Your Pixel can now provide summaries of your longer conversations, so you can see what’s important right away. Now available in German, French, Spanish, Italian, Hindi, and Traditional Chinese. Coming to Pixel Watches soon. 3 Call Screen got an upgrade on Pixel 11 series Whenever you see a call from an unknown number and choose to screen it, Gemini will ask unknown callers why they're reaching out in a much more conversational manner handling the exchange until you decide to jump in or end the call. With a live transcript displayed right on your screen, you can easily follow along and decide exactly when to pick up. Also, coming to Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 soon. 4 Personalize your Pixel with new custom icon styles Following the launch of Custom Icons earlier this year, we’re adding more styles to give you even more ways to personalize your home screen Pixel. Pick from distinct styles that apply across all your app icons on the home screen. 5 New updates coming to Pixel search Now available on Pixel 6 and newer devices, Pixel search helps you find what you need across your phone – from vacation photos and recent emails to messages, calendar events, and device settings. 6 Stay in the moment with Google Messages and HiLight HiLight now supports Google Messages. When your phone is face down, HiLight will glow if you receive a message from one of your favorite contacts — letting you stay present without missing important messages or calls. 7 Keep tabs on your belongings with Pixel Tag Pixel Tag offers peace of mind so you always know where your most important things are — and it’s available November 11. It’s slim enough to fit in your wallet and durable enough to attach to your belongings, with a battery that lasts over a year. The Find Hub network of more than 1 billion Android devices helps you locate your belongings even if they are miles away and UWB enables visual direction and distance guidance to find it nearby. 8 Pixel Tag is available starting November 11 for $29.99 for one or $99.99 for a four-pack. Switch between two of America's best 5G networks with Google Fi Starting today on eligible Pixels, Google Fi’s new super network delivers the nation's fastest, most expansive data coverage by automatically switching between two of America's top 5G cellular networks and millions of secure Wi-Fi networks. 9 10 11 12 Already have a Pixel but not using Google Fi? Get 50% off on select unlimited plans for 12 months. Ends 12/1/26. All terms apply. Visit the blog post , Google Fi website for details, and join Google Fi today . Related Article Google Fi’s new super network Google Fi Wireless is launching a new super network, combining two 5G networks with millions of Wi-Fi networks in one phone plan. See more Unlock your Pixel Watch with your phone Your Pixel devices work better together. When your watch is on your wrist and you’ve unlocked your nearby phone, your Pixel Watch will automatically unlock so you can skip typing your PIN or pattern on the watch. Coming in the next few weeks. 13 Step-by-step workouts are rolling out to Pixel Watch We’re now rolling out step-by-step workouts to Pixel Watch 3 and newer models. Whether you’re following an exercise routine created by your Google Health Coach 14 or a custom workout built in the Google Health app, you can get step-by-step instructions, log reps and weights, and track metrics directly from your Pixel Watch or your phone. Check out our community forum post for the full list of new features arriving on your Pixel devices this month. Posted in:

title: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices
body: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices Nov 10, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Gemini Intelligence is now available on more devices, including motorola signature 27 and Pixel 10. See how expanded capabilities across these devices help you do more. Karthik Thirumalai Product Director, Android AI Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Gemini Intelligence 1 brings the best of Gemini to Android devices, helping your devices work harder for you. Earlier this year, we announced Gemini Intelligence , and this summer devices started rolling out — from the Pixel 11 to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8, Z Flip8 and S26 series. 2 Today, we’re introducing new features built for Gemini Intelligence, and expanding capabilities to more of Android’s most advanced devices . 3 Here’s a look at what’s new. Gemini Intelligence on more devices, including motorola signature 27 and Pixel 10 Gemini Intelligence is coming to even more devices. Motorola is introducing its first Gemini Intelligence device, motorola signature 27 , which is available for pre-order in the U.S. on November 19. And with today’s Pixel Drop , Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro XL, and Pixel 10 Pro Fold get the latest features for Gemini Intelligence. Alongside this expansion, we’re bringing some of our favorite capabilities to more devices and regions, helping handle the busywork so you can focus on what matters. Rambler 4 — which turns spoken thoughts into clean, organized text in real-time — is now available on Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10, Pro XL and Pixel 10 Pro Fold, as well as the new motorola signature 27. And task automation 5 — which lets you ask Gemini to handle logistics like ordering food, hailing rides, or booking reservations across your favorite apps — is expanding to the UK, India, and Japan. Build custom widgets with a prompt Create My Widget 6 , which is rolling out over the next few weeks, lets you design a personalized widget with a simple description in your own words — no coding required. Whether you want a dashboard for your upcoming trip, a monthly spending tracker, or a race day countdown, Create My Widget can pull in information from Gmail, Calendar, and Search to create a custom widget just for you, giving you the information you want at a glance on your homescreen. Get personalized tech support with Device Assistance Device Assistance 7 helps you control, change, or fix your device by just asking your phone for help. Ask Gemini to clear up space on your device, check which apps can access your location, or mute distractions while making sure important calls still come through. Gemini deeply understands your device so it can act as your personal device expert. Experience proactive help across a range of screens Gemini Intelligence is designed to support you across whatever screen you’re using. Last month we launched Googlebook , the first laptop designed for Gemini Intelligence. And if you have a Pixel phone with Gemini Intelligence, it will soon bring proactive suggestions to Android Auto — connecting the dots across your apps to surface helpful, personalized suggestions 8 when you need them. For example, if your friend texts you to ask where you are meeting for a pilates class, Gemini Intelligence on Android Auto can find your confirmation email and instantly suggest sending the address with a single tap. Plus, in the next few weeks, Create My Widget is coming to Pixel Watch. You’ll be able to design widgets that keep the details that matter to you right on your wrist. Get the latest news from Google in your inbox Sign up for our newsletters with product updates, event information, special offers, and more. Done. Just one step more. Check your inbox to confirm your subscription. You can also subscribe with a different email address . Your information will be used in accordance with Google's privacy policy. You may opt out at any time. Posted in:
